kind: live estimate: made during or after voting, with election-day information; not the sealed prediction
used: Made during voting, before the polls closed, from the official turnout reports and election-day reporting.
key_inputs: 2026-10-25 18:57 CET: supplied sealed prior anchors vote shares and uncertainty; SNS 47.0%, students 41.1%, turnout 64.6%, SNS most-seats probability 75.5%, SNS majority probability 45.8%.

2026-10-25 14:31 CET, N1: RIK turnout at noon was 34.55%, versus 21.33% in 2023; CRTA turnout at 13:00 was 41.1% ±0.9 percentage points, versus 26.6%; CeSID/Ipsos turnout at 14:00 was 46.4%, versus 32.2%. These are correlated observations of one turnout surge, not independent partisan signals.

2026-10-25 15:00 CET, RIK briefing reproduced by the Serbian government: turnout at 14:00 was 46.53%; Vojvodina 49.23%, Belgrade 47.55%, Sumadija and western Serbia 44.95%, southern and eastern Serbia 44.04%.

2026-10-25 17:00 CET, CRTA: turnout at 16:00 was 56.4% ±0.9 percentage points, compared with its reported 42.1% in 2023; pressures were reported at 29% of polling stations and voting-integrity irregularities at 17%. Irregularity reports increase uncertainty but cannot be converted into a quantified vote adjustment.

2026-10-25 17:28 CET, RTV/Tanjug update reporting RIK: turnout at 16:00 was 56.38%; Vojvodina 58.76%, Belgrade 57.68%, Sumadija and western Serbia 55.29%, southern and eastern Serbia 53.34%. Agreement with CRTA strengthens the turnout evidence; regional levels alone do not identify party preferences.

2026-10-25 17:10 CET, 021 reporting CeSID/Ipsos: turnout at 17:00 was 60.8% on a sample of 750 polling stations. Vijesti's 17:21 CET entry compares this with 47.2% at the same hour in 2023 and 58.77% final turnout; adding the full historical late increment would imply 72.4%, discounted here for possible earlier voting and a shrinking turnout advantage.

2023-12-17 20:47 CET, historical CeSID/Ipsos projection reported by Insajder: at 88.4% sample completion, SNS was estimated at 46.2% and 128 seats; RIK's final result, reported 2024-01-12, was 46.75% and 129 seats. This supports substantial weight for mature sample counts once available, but supplies no vote-share observation for today's pre-close estimate.

2026-10-25 19:17 CET evidence cutoff: no verified exit poll, national vote projection or partial official vote count was found; no independently verified national 18:00 or 19:00 turnout release was available in the retrieved sources. Post-cutoff evidence is excluded.

Analytical assumptions at completion: turnout evidence prompts a modest 1.4-point reduction in SNS and 1.9-point increase in students, with broad uncertainty because additional voters' preferences are unobserved. Correlated share scenarios retain approximately the prior's main-party uncertainty and include threshold crossings when estimating seat probabilities.

Seat-calculation assumptions at completion: D'Hondt is applied to individual lists, with the 3% votes-cast threshold converted using an estimated 2.5% invalid share and minority quotients multiplied by 1.35. The unobserved eight-list composition of other_minority is assumed to be 0.80, 0.60, 0.45, 0.30, 0.10, 0.07, 0.05 and 0.03 percent of valid votes; the displayed seats are conditional on this split. The invalid-share estimate is informed by approximately 2.9% invalid ballots in 2023, not a count from today.

sources.used_for: Morning and early-afternoon turnout comparisons with 2023.
Official national and regional turnout at 14:00.
Primary observer turnout estimate, sampling margin, historical comparison and irregularities.
RIK national and regional turnout at 16:00; nine minority lists.
CeSID/Ipsos 17:00 turnout estimate and sample size.
2023 turnout at 17:00 and final turnout for late-day extrapolation.
Final 2023 result against which the historical projection is compared.

sources.published: Publication time not stated; historical 2023 results

notes: The evidence cutoff is 19:17 CET, before polls close, so this remains a prior-based estimate without observed party results. Strong turnout raises expected final participation and supports only a modest, judgmental shift toward students; turnout does not establish who additional voters support. Earlier releases recalibrate the supplied prior rather than count as independent news since 18:57, and wide 80% ranges reflect that limitation. Seat totals are a conditional central scenario, with substantial uncertainty from SPS crossing the threshold and the unknown distribution among minority lists.
